what: evidence that the ledger face has been on a screen, not only through a headless dump
why: req/02 W15 clause 3: each face must carry a record of having mounted in a real window (headless is not the window). §495 landed the module-graph fix (tokens.mjs's runtime node:fs read moved to build time) and proved a headless mount, but left the non-headless run, the styled screenshot, and this record as the residual work under F-1.
how: faces/ledger/tools/browser-mount-smoke.mjs's fixture (browser-mount.html + browser-mount-entry.mjs) is served over http by a static server rooted at the project, now also answering /s-common/tokens.css from the one stylesheet of record (parts/tools/token-source.mjs), the same route name shell/tools/serve.mjs answers. faces/ledger/tools/real-window-smoke.mjs starts that server, then shells out to shell/tools/real_window.ps1 -- the shell's own real-window instrument, reused rather than duplicated -- which opens Chrome in app mode, reads the window's own title back through the Win32 window list, and photographs the window rectangle off the screen. The element/row count and theme are computed inside the page by browser-mount-entry.mjs and written into document.title, so the numbers in this record are the numbers the page computed, not ones typed here.

readByEye.byWhom: the agent that wrote this record, looking at both pictures at full resolution
held: the stylesheet of record is applied, not the smoke page's old inline #0B0C0D/#E8EAEC placeholder: dark reads as a near-black ground with a warm off-white ink and a muted secondary tone for the meta lines; light reads as a warm ivory ground with dark ink, not a flat colour-inversion of dark
the Deny badge is drawn in the same red in both themes, and 'undo' keeps its own bordered box in both -- a token, not a hand-picked colour per theme
no text is printed over other text anywhere in either capture

no row and no glyph is cut off mid-character; the two rows visible in the 900px-tall window (write/Admit, delete/Deny) are shown in full including their open notes, and the page's own vertical scrollbar is the only sign more content exists below the fold, which is the row layout behaving as declared (fixed-pitch rows that do not reflow) rather than a clipping defect

the window itself is a real OS window: native title bar with minimize/maximize/close controls and the browser's own tab-loading icon are visible in both captures, which a headless dump cannot show and a screenshot of a maximized full-bleed page could be mistaken for
